scope: Owned Linux CPU fixtures for actual forced-termination and archived-record inspection; no model inference.

child-kill.target: Owned experiment child after witnessed CPU work and an initial running record

recorder-kill.target: Owned recorder after witnessed CPU work and an initial running record
recorder-kill.cleanup: Adopt and reap only the child in the original owned recorder process group; preserve the unfinished record.

success.target: Fresh CPU work in each actual recording

acceptance: Validate the source Git commit and all 148 pinned package files before copying the reader/recorder payload.
Lock each independent condition offline and commit its actual fixture inputs before running.
Check nonce, parent PID, process group and session before targeting an experiment child.
Check actual run IDs, child work, recorded states and real process exits.
Source schema-2 unfinished records retain pre-child baselines and unknown final input state.
List and show actual records; export each explicit historical run; exercise self-diff or the two fresh successful controls.
Source outcome filters exclude unfinished running records from both success and failure; latest-successful selects the two actual successful controls.
All archived run-directory bytes remain unchanged during inspection; all owned processes are cleaned up.
limitations: This is SIGKILL on a Linux process, not a power-loss, filesystem-durability or GPU-inference experiment.
A running record after recorder loss is incomplete evidence, without a confirmed final child outcome.
The controller performs bounded cleanup; no automatic recovery or repair is attributed to ReproLLM.
Released 0.6.1 does not gain source-only filters or schema-2 baselines.
